source.title: PaCE: Parsimonious Concept Engineering for Large Language Models
source.authors: Jinqi Luo; Tianjiao Ding; Kwan Ho Ryan Chan; D. Thaker; Aditya Chattopadhyay; Chris Callison-Burch; René Vidal

record.tranche_reason: The paper extends concept-direction analysis to LLaMA activations and reports semantic geometry and retrieval results relevant to indirect LLM evidence; it does not reproduce the toy-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper measures semantic organization and retrieval among its LLM concept vectors. Its detoxification, faithfulness, sentiment, and ablation scores evaluate PaCE's alignment method, not feature recovery or superposition, so those results are not rows. The paper's single-vector representation choice and discussion of multi-vector alternatives are not comparative tests.
record.test_reason: PaCE treats LLM activations as sparse combinations of a supervised concept dictionary and uses this as an alignment tool. It reports its own alignment performance. Its geometry analysis covers semantic clustering and retrieval among concept directions built by representation reading (contrastive stimuli plus PCA). That analysis does not measure superposition, neuron-level feature spread, or unsupervised (SAE) recovery of sparse features. Semantic organization of concept vectors is a related but different construct, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The authors' main conclusion is that PaCE gives state-of-the-art training-free alignment while largely keeping linguistic capability, on detoxification, faithfulness and sentiment tasks. They do this by sparse-coding activations over a large concept dictionary and removing the undesirable components. As a secondary point, they observe semantically structured clusters of concept directions in LLaMA2-13B-Chat and conjecture this generalizes to other LLMs. The multi-vector remark is a limitation or future-work note, not a conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Uses concept directions extracted from LLM activations, a large PaCE dictionary, sparse coding, and semantic clustering/retrieval; it does not use toy networks or reproduce the original toy-model interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The geometry analysis is reported for LLaMA2-13B-Chat and the first 10,000 PaCE-1M concepts; the authors conjecture that similar semantic structure generalizes to other LLMs, but do not test that here.

fits_no_version.finding: Supervised concept directions for 10,000 words in LLaMA2-13B-Chat form semantically coherent clusters: UMAP plot, a block-diagonal EnSC affinity over 200 clusters, and similarity retrieval. The authors also state that the concept directions are non-orthogonal and often linearly dependent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept directions extracted by representation reading in LLMs are organized semantically and are mutually non-orthogonal.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says the source code will be released soon. Dataset URL: https://github.com/peterljq/Parsimonious-Concept-Engineering
record.problems: The geometry evidence is qualitative and uses PaCE's GPT-generated stimuli and extracted concept directions rather than independently verified features. The reported geometry analysis focuses on one model; there are no uncertainty estimates or ground-truth feature-recovery measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant geometry rows omitted. Alignment benchmark and ablation results in Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix B.5 are excluded because they evaluate PaCE's performance rather than measuring the claim's feature geometry.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no phase transition, no geometry of superposed features.
Does not examine neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
Does not examine causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measure of features spread across neurons. No unsupervised dictionary or SAE recovery of sparse features. The dictionary is built from GPT-4 stimuli per word.
Does not assess completeness, stability or canonicity of dictionary atoms. The atoms are supervised concept directions, not learned SAE features.
Uses one vector per concept by convention. Multi-vector or subspace alternatives are raised only as future work (B.7).

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T3' and its V4 'supports' label are not justified. The dictionary atoms come from supervised contrastive PCA, not unsupervised sparse dictionary learning, and no superposition quantity is measured. The Toy Models paper is cited only in B.7 as motivation for multi-vector concept representations.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-to-dimension capacity sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric phases are tested.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test other causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests semantic organization and retrieval of PaCE dictionary directions in LLaMA2-13B-Chat, not neuron-level feature distribution, SAE feature recovery, or generalization across a broad set of LLMs.
Does not test whether dictionary atoms are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model's representation.
Uses one vector per concept but does not compare this representation with multi-vector or multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-13B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: Visualized concept vectors with UMAP and examined semantic clusters.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic organization of concept vectors
rows.value: The text reports that semantically similar concept vectors appear close and that several semantic groups are separated into distinct clusters.
rows.note: Qualitative visualization; no numerical clustering or feature-recovery score is reported.
rows.check: A UMAP plot of supervised RepE concept directions shows semantic clustering. That is not evidence that features are spread across neurons or recoverable as sparse dictionary features, so it does not bear on V4. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Applied Elastic Net Subspace Clustering to concept vectors.
rows.measure: Affinity structure and cluster separation among concept vectors
rows.value: The reported affinity matrix has a block-diagonal structure; the authors describe points from different clusters as separated and points within a cluster as close.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative structure, not a numerical clustering-quality measure.
rows.check: The subject is LLaMA2-13B-Chat (B.4: all LLaMA-2 models are the chat version), not the base model. A block-diagonal EnSC affinity among concept directions measures semantic grouping, not superposition or feature recovery.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-13B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: Retrieved concept vectors by similarity to a target concept.
rows.measure: Semantic relevance of retrieved vectors to the target concept
rows.value: The text identifies affection and friendship as geometrically close and semantically relevant to love.
rows.note: No numerical similarity values are given in the text.
rows.check: Retrieving neighbours of 'love' by similarity shows semantic proximity of concept vectors only. It does not bear on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PaCE concept vectors measured in LLaMA2-13B-Chat
reader_labels.reason: The reported clustering and retrieval results show semantic organization among dictionary directions in this tested model (r1–r3); this is indirect evidence, not a test of neuron-level distribution or SAE recovery.
